resolution.title: Improved session availability test
resolution.description: The core PHP session test of PrestaShop checks if the sessions directory is writable, which does not always work as expected. Combined with an `open_basedir` configured without the `session.save_path`, PHP sessions are still working as intended, but the test_sessions function fails. In such a case, the One Click Upgrade module will fail checking its prerequisites in an attempt to make an upgrade. A fix was already opened for the autoupgrade module itself, but it should be also fixed in the core.
resolution.how_to_test: Have a PrestaShop 1.6 or higher. Configure open_basedir and don't include session.save_path. Go to Module list > Upgrade One Click Upgrade to 4.15.0 > Configure the module, then see the error.

resolution.title: Module from theme with tab using SF routing fails after enabling the theme
resolution.description: When a theme installs a module that contains a tab with route_name it redirects to the theme index right away But for the route to be usable the cache needs to be cleared, this operation is handled in a shutdown callback which is why when the page is refreshed at first the cache still has not been cleared yet This results in an exception as the route can not be found, to avoid this blocking exception during the menu rendering we catch the `RouteNotFoundException` and the associated tab is not rendered, after a few seconds when the cache is cleared the page can be refreshed and the tab will be displayed appropriately Additionally during the tests it was found that the INSTALL event for module is triggered even when it failed, this can result in unwanted added tab even if the module failed to install, so now the event is only triggered on install success  **Note**: this is not an ideal fix but so far I didn't find a proper way to correctly clear the cache without causing side effects bugs on refresh
resolution.author: jolelievre

ticket.title: Bad default value for "Product::pack_stock_type" - Inheritance issue when loading Pack class (that inherit Product)
ticket.bug:
The default value of Product::pack_stock_type is set as "Pack::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT;" which in turn has a default value PackStockType::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT.

This is an inheritance issue because Pack class inherit product so when a Pack class is instantiated before the class loader attempt to load the Product class. Before of all the class loader assign valued to class field and the value from Product::pack_stock_type is a field of Pack ... that is the class i attempt to instantiate at the beginning..

In normal situation this issue pass unnoticed because in class_index.php the class is loaded by alphabetic order but is pure luck.
In certain specific situation this may conduce to an error of "ClassNotFoundException".
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9608268/178926510-92a88007-89bf-44f3-9577-f2c56f1c8e5e.png)

The solution is to load directly the default value as "Product::pack_stock_type = PackStockType::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT;".

in fact all the other fields of products ha similar default value ex:
public $out_of_stock = OutOfStockType::OUT_OF_STOCK_DEFAULT;
public $redirect_type = RedirectType::TYPE_NOT_FOUND;

resolution.title: Change default assignation of Product::pack_stock_type
resolution.description: changed default assignation of Product::pack_stock_type for exclude loading error of Pack class (inheritance issue).
resolution.author: abramofranchetti

resolution.title: Improved session availability test
resolution.description: The core PHP session test of PrestaShop checks if the sessions directory is writable, which does not always work as expected. Combined with an `open_basedir` configured without the `session.save_path`, PHP sessions are still working as intended, but the test_sessions function fails. In such a case, the One Click Upgrade module will fail checking its prerequisites in an attempt to make an upgrade. A fix was already opened for the autoupgrade module itself, but it should be also fixed in the core.

resolution.title: Module from theme with tab using SF routing fails after enabling the theme
resolution.description: When a theme installs a module that contains a tab with route_name it redirects to the theme index right away But for the route to be usable the cache needs to be cleared, this operation is handled in a shutdown callback which is why when the page is refreshed at first the cache still has not been cleared yet This results in an exception as the route can not be found, to avoid this blocking exception during the menu rendering we catch the `RouteNotFoundException` and the associated tab is not rendered, after a few seconds when the cache is cleared the page can be refreshed and the tab will be displayed appropriately Additionally during the tests it was found that the INSTALL event for module is triggered even when it failed, this can result in unwanted added tab even if the module failed to install, so now the event is only triggered on install success  **Note**: this is not an ideal fix but so far I didn't find a proper way to correctly clear the cache without causing side effects bugs on refresh
resolution.author: jolelievre

i don't understand why the core is doing this but i'm facing an infinite loop when customer is loggedin but its totally logical if I read the code. First it was working but since I hooked a module on actionObjectUpdateAfter i get this syndrom.

I searched in code and this is what i found

When we are logged in as customer on front, 
It calls 
1. Hook::exec 
which check user logged in groups in Hook class with the method 
2. getHookModuleExecList who calls
3. getAllHookRegistrations.
This function calls

5. Context::getContext()->cookie->isSessionAlive()
this function calls (on cookie class)
6. $this->getSession($this->session_id)
and the getSession method calls 
7. $session->save() 
who calls in object model the 
8. update() method who calls the 
9. hook actionObjectUpdateAfter who tried to Hook::exec

```
if(get_class($this) != 'EmployeeSession' && get_class($this) != 'CustomerSession'){

}

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/79b15c0b0ad54e6eafc58841ecf3f889957b9384/src/Core/Module/ModuleManager.php#L348

ticket.title: Bad default value for "Product::pack_stock_type" - Inheritance issue when loading Pack class (that inherit Product)
ticket.bug:
The default value of Product::pack_stock_type is set as "Pack::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT;" which in turn has a default value PackStockType::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT.

This is an inheritance issue because Pack class inherit product so when a Pack class is instantiated before the class loader attempt to load the Product class. Before of all the class loader assign valued to class field and the value from Product::pack_stock_type is a field of Pack ... that is the class i attempt to instantiate at the beginning..

In normal situation this issue pass unnoticed because in class_index.php the class is loaded by alphabetic order but is pure luck.
In certain specific situation this may conduce to an error of "ClassNotFoundException".
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9608268/178926510-92a88007-89bf-44f3-9577-f2c56f1c8e5e.png)

The solution is to load directly the default value as "Product::pack_stock_type = PackStockType::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT;".

in fact all the other fields of products ha similar default value ex:
public $out_of_stock = OutOfStockType::OUT_OF_STOCK_DEFAULT;
public $redirect_type = RedirectType::TYPE_NOT_FOUND;

resolution.title: Change default assignation of Product::pack_stock_type
resolution.description: changed default assignation of Product::pack_stock_type for exclude loading error of Pack class (inheritance issue).
resolution.author: abramofranchetti
